feasible.reason: The headline countermeasure (a) does not defend against the stated threat; it defeats only the as-built 2019 implant and fails under Kerckhoffs. Bypass 1 (bus tap): PQ1 firmware AND the glyph atlas are public (open-source policy; atlas is a reproducible NS-slot blob at a fixed offset, nonsecure/assets/ui-px/atlas.pq1a, 75,128 B). An implant author therefore has every glyph variant; a per-session sub-cell x/y offset is defeated by a sliding correlator over the few-pixel jitter range (26 templates x <=14x22 cell x ~25 offsets is trivial for any implant MCU), and colour-LSB jitter is defeated by thresholding the RGB565 high bits. This is not 'raises cost' in any measurable sense: a sliding/threshold matcher is a few hundred bytes more code and no observable power/size delta for D-03 to see. The proposal itself cites the Ledger 1.6 'randomised screen-update parameters' precedent being found insufficient — same failure class. Bypass 2 (EM/camera averaging over refresh): the Kuhn PET-2004 countermeasure works on an FPD-link that re-transmits pixel data EVERY refresh, so per-frame randomisation prevents averaging. The NV3007 is a GRAM-backed panel (lcd_nv3007.rs:46-49, 651): the SPI bus carries a frame once per paint and the panel self-refreshes from static GRAM. A per-SESSION jitter is constant across every panel refresh in that session, so averaging within the session is unaffected. Making it per-refresh means repainting continuously (~48.6 ms/frame at 20 MHz, lcd_nv3007.rs:203), which multiplies bus-tap exposure (contradicting leg 1) and is the tempo regime #258 already showed failing on glass; panel-internal driver/rail emission is F-24 stage E sub-channels 2/3, accepted as hardware-only (shield/regulator), which the proposal does not flag as kind=hardware/mixed. (c) dimming addresses no information leak: the AW99703 is a constant-current sink whose draw and 1 MHz boost emission are content-independent, and a camera auto-exposes; it only helps against a human shoulder-surfer while costing legibility. Only (b) one-word reveal and (d) the warning page are sound, and both are UX/optical-residual items already enumerated in gh #237 and in Trezor (reset.c:206-231, en.json:2248) — they are not 'beyond' and do nothing against a passive bus tap, which records all 24 frames regardless of paging or hold jitter. Feasibility also overstated: (a) lives only in the ui-px compositor, which is 76,949 B over the 466,944 B secure slot and excluded from make release, so the shipping image today renders the seed via the legacy 16x4 secret_text path, which would need a paired twin (paired-constants rule).
feasible.corrections: Salvage as a P3 UX/optical item under #237, not a P2 security improvement: (1) Keep (b) one-word-per-page (Trezor One precedent verified; the existing scroll-to-end/seen_last gate in show_mnemonic_simple adapts to 24 pages) and (d) the never-digital warning (one show_status line next to seed_wizard.rs:333, fits 16 chars on the legacy row as 'Never store it digitally'). State honestly that these reduce per-photo/shoulder yield only. Drop the random 0-300 ms pre-display hold or justify it: a passive implant triggers on CS/RAMWR itself, nothing is host-aligned. (2) Drop or re-label (a): if kept, claim only 'breaks a byte-exact fixed-offset matcher such as the 2019 Ledger implant; a sliding/threshold matcher bypasses it; zero effect against the panel's own refresh'. If implemented anyway, the TRNG offset must be a public (non-secret-dependent) value applied uniformly across the union box so blit_secret_run's data-independent access pattern survives; K glyph variants multiply the per-pixel 26-candidate scan by K and need a designer-supplied second face, not just atlas budget; colour-LSB jitter under a D-04 constant-weight RGB565 encoding must be weight-preserving (pair flips), which shrinks it further. (3) Re-type the EM/camera-averaging leg as kind=hardware (display-module shield, isolated panel/backlight regulator) per F-24 stage E sub-channels 2/3; no firmware per-session jitter touches it on a GRAM panel. (4) (c) is cosmetic: add it only as a user-comfort option (write REG_LEDLSB then REG_LEDMSB via a new pub fn in aw99703.rs; ~10 lines, pq1-only, iota2 bench has no panel so it is untestable there) and do not list it as a leakage countermeasure. (5) Cost: (b)+(d) are S, not M; (a) is M-L once the legacy twin, atlas regeneration (make ui-px-assets re-pins ATLAS_ROOT) and the ui-px flash lever are counted, and it cannot ship until ui-px fits the secure slot. (6) Unverified citation: the '0x4D00-0x4E40 a-z templates' detail from the Grand Idea Studio slides was not checked here; treat as a lead.

vendor-claim.reason: Every load-bearing precedent claim checks out against the actual code/sources: Trezor One shows one word per frame (legacy/firmware/reset.c:206-231 via layoutResetWord, legacy/firmware/layout2.c:785); Trezor core ships the "Never put your backup anywhere digital." warning (core/translations/en.json:2248) and shows it BEFORE the words (core/src/apps/management/reset_device/layout.py:180 then :189); the Ledger implant stores a-z glyph templates at 0x4D00-0x4E40 and template-matches the OLED SPI stream (Joe Grand slides, text lines 193-207); Ledger's 2019 countermeasure randomised "contrast, power supply, frequency of oscillation" and was declared insufficient on the Nano X / Nano S Plus screen in the 2023 new-pin-screen post; Kuhn PET 2004 literally says the only effective software protection "appears to be the addition of random bits to the color combinations" and that a glyph-cache reuse "merely assists the eavesdropper". All six repo_evidence items are accurate (paging 8/3 per page, gate at :333, no photo/digital string, brightness constants written once in configure(), fixed SECRET_ADV=14 cells, #258 and #237 OPEN as described). No vendor was found shipping glyph geometry/colour-LSB jitter or K glyph variants (searched Ledger/Trezor/Keystone/BitBox/Coldcard; Trezor core has no randomisation in any share_words component), so 'beyond' holds for part (a). The precedent is incomplete rather than false: one-word-per-screen is a CURRENT shipping Trezor feature (Safe 5/delizia and Safe 7/eckhart), not just legacy; Coldcard ships random masking-noise pixels on the seed screen; the 'Ledger 1.6' version label is not supported by any fetched source; and the proposal's 'per-session' jitter contradicts Kuhn's own per-placement requirement.
vendor-claim.corrections: (1) Part (b) one-word-per-frame is NOT 'beyond' but vendor parity: besides Trezor One (legacy, which also runs TWO passes — 'Write down the seed' then 'Please check the seed', reset.c:206 `for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++)`, layout2.c:801-805), current Trezor Safe 5 (layout_delizia/component/share_words.rs:21 'contains one word per screen') and Safe 7 (layout_eckhart/firmware/share_words.rs:210, same wording) ship one word per screen today. Trezor Safe 3 (caesar) uses 3/page and Model T (bolt) 4/page. Trezor has NO random pre-display hold in any share_words component (grep 'random' in all four share_words.rs: zero hits), so the random 0-300 ms hold part of (b) remains novel. (2) Part (c) wizard backlight dim has no Trezor precedent: Trezor defines BacklightLevels DIM/LOW (core/embed/rust/src/ui/layout_eckhart/theme/backlight.rs:6-7, LOW=116 DIM=43) but uses them only for inactivity autodim (core/src/trezor/power_management/autodim.py:16) and orientation change (core/src/apps/common/lock_manager.py:299), never during backup/share-word display — so (c) is genuinely 'beyond' in vendor terms. (3) Part (d) warning: Trezor CORE only (bolt/caesar/delizia/eckhart reset.py via show_warning_backup), shown before the share words (reset_device/layout.py:180 before :189); Trezor One legacy has no such page (grep digital/photo in legacy/firmware/*.c: nothing). Add the warning's exact string and key: TR.reset__never_make_digital_copy = 'Never put your backup anywhere digital.' (en.json:2248). (4) Ledger implant precedent should say Nano X, not generic 'Ledger': slides are 'Reverse Engineering a Ledger Nano X Hardware Implant', Joe Grand, hardwear.io 2026 (first seen Reddit Aug 2025); implant monitors the SE↔OLED SPI bus, template matches a-z glyphs stored at 0x4D00-0x4E40, stores recovered seed at flash 0x7000, exfiltrates over 4G LTE; slide also says 'New iterations of implant have already been spotted'. (5) 'Ledger 1.6': the ledger.com/blog/oled-vuln post (08/07/2019, reporter Christian Reitter, CVE-2019-14354) names no firmware version, only 'regular firmware updates ... scheduled for Q4 of 2019'; the countermeasure wording is 'continuously and randomly modifying physical parameters such as contrast, power supply, frequency of oscillation' PLUS 'all sensitive information (recovery phrase, PIN digits) will be displayed within boxes in inverted pixel mode'. Drop the '1.6' label or source it from Ledger release notes; the 'insufficient on the next panel' claim is confirmed verbatim by new-pin-screen ('on the new screen model, this countermeasure was observed to be insufficient ... no amount of physical noise could efficiently hide the dependency'). (6) Kuhn attribution and a design correction: Kuhn PET 2004 (text p.12-13, 18) covers randomised low-order RGB bits, NOT randomised glyph shapes/positions; glyph-shape randomisation is Kuhn & Anderson 1998 Soft Tempest fonts (the 1998 font package uses 'minor random variations of the glyph shapes'). More importantly Kuhn requires the random bits to be 'randomly selected each time a new character is placed on the screen' and explicitly says reusing an already-randomised bitmap 'merely assists the eavesdropper' — a PER-SESSION fixed jitter (as the proposal words it) defeats the byte-exact template matcher but, if the wizard repaints the same jittered frame periodically, it re-creates exactly the cached-glyph failure Kuhn warns about against periodic averaging. Jitter must be re-drawn per placement/per repaint (or the frame painted once and held) to claim the Kuhn countermeasure. (7) Adjacent vendor precedent missing: Coldcard v2.1.2 (blog.coinkite.com/noise-troll) added 'masking noise along the right hand side of the screen' with 'a large amount of random noise on each line' on the seed-word screen (plus masked PIN echo) — this is the 'random pad pixels' candidate listed in #237 and is prior art for the random-colour/noise half of (a), though not for glyph geometry jitter or K variants. (8) Repo detail: brightness constants are at secure/src/hw/aw99703.rs:113-115 (not 66-69/78) and are written in configure() at :546-547; aw99703.rs:66-69 are the register-map constants. font.rs:233-238 confirmed (SECRET_CELLS=8, SECRET_ADV=14; cell centre at :299). Gate at seed_wizard.rs:333 confirmed; paging at :64-82 confirmed (PX 8/page, legacy 3/page).
